prompt:
Render one full-fidelity desktop website comp, landscape 3:2, edge to edge, crisp readable text, no browser chrome. This is The Lobby’s Privacy page: a short public note people revisit to understand information use.

Lead with a narrow topic index beside one continuous calm reading column. Compact masthead “The Lobby”, ordinary “Back to The Lobby” link, then “Privacy” and “How The Lobby uses information when you visit, sign in, and use its Tools.” The index repeats the seven section headings as conventional text links. Reading column uses these exact headings and paragraphs in order:

Visiting
The Schedule Downloader is open without signing in.

Signing in
We keep your email address, Tool access, and a sign-in session so you can return to your Tools. The sign-in cookie lasts up to 90 days and renews while you use the site.

Remembered teams
Members can save teams and use a replaceable private calendar link.

Connecting Google Calendar
Google asks for permission to view and edit events across your calendars. The Lobby changes only events it adds in the calendar you choose.

Your choices
You can replace your Member link or disconnect your calendar. Disconnecting removes upcoming games The Lobby added; played games stay.

Running the site
AWS and Cloudflare help run and protect The Lobby. Basic service logs and counts of calendar use help keep it working.

Leaving The Lobby
Removing membership deletes the access record and Remembered teams.

Use the reference only for navy linework, seafoam palette, Rubik headings, Nunito Sans prose, and the existing robot: no greeting hero, sun, foliage, wave, grain, or Sign in button. Pale seafoam reading ground, real body size and readable measure. Thin navy rules own the frame; plain prose stays unboxed. Quiet footer with a tiny decorative robot. No invented dates, contacts, controls, or claims.
